notes: Position 10 D1 was a raw Official nonpass attributed to external PyPI SSL EOF.
Position 22 D2 passed controlled qualification, but both Official attempts were infrastructure-censored.
Position 22 D2 had neither an adjudicated qualification nor Official outcome and failed the run audit.
Position 23 D2 Official-passed, but qualification and exact retry were infrastructure-censored; its run failed the audit and is not a primary terminal outcome.

outcome_accounting.cross_arm_terminal_judgment: P preserved success in every cell, but R0 and R1 had no adjudicated algorithm failure. Infrastructure censoring prevents a terminal-success superiority claim.

model_usage.accounting: All model usage from scheduled arm executions is retained, including infrastructure-censored trials; controller-only setup attempts and exact zero-model retries add zero tokens.

comparisons.interpretation: P reduced input tokens against full-history R1 but not against ordinary replay R0. P also used more output tokens than R0, so it does not dominate R0 under the preregistered split token accounting.

secondary_measurement.reason: Arms ran sequentially and encountered unequal package-cache, resolver, acquisition, and censoring conditions. Wall-time differences are descriptive and are not used to infer an algorithm advantage.

causal_findings.finding: Minimal explicit project state did not outperform ordinary successful-program reuse.
causal_findings.evidence: P had no terminal-success advantage over adjudicated R0 outcomes and used 6.6% more total input tokens, 90.2% more D2 input tokens, and 12.6% more output tokens than R0.
causal_findings.scope: Four consumed/Dev projects under same-condition and adjacent-supported-Python deployment.

causal_findings.finding: Full completed session history is an inefficient default reuse mechanism.
causal_findings.evidence: R1 used 2.57 times R0 total input tokens without an adjudicated terminal-success advantage; passing D1 preflights still triggered model work that often returned identical or semantically equivalent programs.
causal_findings.scope: The fixed R1 policy always requested improvement, so the claim concerns this full-history policy rather than every possible history summarizer.

causal_findings.finding: A successful bootstrap program is reusable but not temporally stable.
causal_findings.evidence: At position 23 D1, the same retained program passed P and R1 preflight but later failed R0 through dependency backtracking into an obsolete Shapely build. At other positions, repeated package acquisition also alternated between success and infrastructure errors.
causal_findings.scope: This is execution evidence for resolver and acquisition drift, not a causal arm advantage because runs were sequential rather than simultaneous.

causal_findings.finding: Official success does not identify a unique deployment path.
causal_findings.evidence: Official-passing programs varied in retry logic, environment mechanism, version constraints, and installed extras. These differences are retained as path-quality annotations and do not override the Official outcome.
causal_findings.scope: Path completeness and robustness are secondary analyses, with EnvBench Official remaining the terminal authority.

stage_decision.promotion_rule: P must preserve terminal success and reduce new model inference against both R0 and R1.
stage_decision.reason: P preserved terminal success and beat R1 input usage, but it did not reduce input or output tokens against R0 and did not establish a success advantage.

next_review_questions: Should the next experiment target fixed real Official bad cases where ordinary replay plus repair fails, rather than another broad state representation?
Should temporal resolver and acquisition drift be treated as an observed environment condition with repeated trials, rather than repaired through more cross-candidate rules?
Can a failure-triggered strong Agent be given a better stopping objective that avoids unnecessary exploration while preserving Official success?
